_: Copy this to .kbfix.json in your project, or to ~/.kbfix.json for the whole machine. Project wins over home. Every field is optional; what is shown here is the default.
_layouts: Which layouts to consider. Omit it and every installed layout is active (see layouts/). Narrowing the list makes detection faster and safer: if you never type Russian, leaving it out removes a whole class of candidate reading. The pre-0.2 form {"pair": "en-he"} is still understood and means the same as ["en", "he"].
_directions: Which transpositions to allow, as "from->to". Omit it for all of them. Use it to switch one off, for example to detect Hebrew typed on the English layout but never the reverse.
_minSignalChars: Below this many letters there is not enough evidence either way, so it says nothing. Lowering it will start guessing at things like /pr.
_minTargetScore: How much the transposed text has to read like real prose, 0 to 1.
_minMargin: How far the transposition has to beat the text as typed. This is the gate that keeps ordinary prompts safe, because real prose scores near 1 in its own language and nothing can beat it by this much.
_minCandidateGap: How far the best reading has to beat the second-best. Only bites with three or more layouts: a Latin string can read plausibly as both Hebrew and Russian, and when it does, neither answer is safe to give. Raising all three thresholds makes it quieter; lowering them makes it guess.
